$comment:
SAMPLE LANGUAGE FOR EVERY PLACEHOLDER.

A placeholder value is dropped VERBATIM into legal prose. Whether it reads correctly is entirely a question of the form it was stored in, and nothing about the field name says which form is wanted.

Write 3000000 into insuranceCglLimit and the clause reads "insurance of not less than 3000000". Write 20 into colocationSharePct and it reads "a share equal to 20 of the revenue". Both load, both validate, both are wrong in a way that survives to an executed document — because the number is right and only the drafting is broken.

So every placeholder here carries the form its value must take, and a fragment showing how the sentence reads once it is filled. The drafter quotes the sample back when a placeholder is unresolved, which turns "no value in the deal file" into something a person can act on.

DEFINED TERMS ARE DIFFERENT and are marked so. Their value is not a house choice at all: it is whatever THIS lease calls the thing. Read it off the document during the audit and do not tidy it — a lease that says Lessor does not become Landlord because Landlord reads better.

placeholders.name: LandlordTitle
placeholders.source: definedTerms.LandlordTitle.value — read off the base lease
placeholders.renders: …{{LandlordTitle}} shall not permit… → LESSOR shall not permit…
placeholders.note: Whatever the lease calls it. Landlord, Lessor, Owner, Licensor. Substituting the one you prefer puts two vocabularies in one document and invites an argument about whether they mean the same person.

placeholders.name: TenantTitle
placeholders.renders: …{{TenantTitle}} may terminate… → LESSEE may terminate…
placeholders.note: Tenant, Lessee, Licensee. Same rule.

placeholders.name: RentName
placeholders.renders: …the {{RentName}} shall increase… → the Annual Rent shall increase…
placeholders.note: Frequently NOT "Rent". Lease Fee, Monthly Rent, Rental, Annual Rent. Introducing "Rent" where the lease says something else creates two payment obligations on one document.

placeholders.name: TermName
placeholders.renders: …the {{TermName}} is extended… → the Term is extended…
placeholders.note: Capitalised as the lease capitalises it.

placeholders.name: ExtensionName
placeholders.renders: …four additional {{ExtensionName}}s… → four additional Renewal Terms…
placeholders.note: Extension Term, Renewal Term, extension period. Note the clause text adds the plural 's' — a value already plural reads as "Renewal Termss".

placeholders.name: AreaName
placeholders.renders: …access to the {{AreaName}}… → access to the Premises…
placeholders.note: The leased area. Check it against PropertyName: one lease in the sample set inverted the two, so "Property" meant the leased area and "LESSOR'S Property" the wider parcel.

placeholders.name: PropertyName
placeholders.renders: …any other occupant of the {{PropertyName}}… → any other occupant of the Property…
placeholders.note: The landlord's wider land. Used undefined by several clauses, so the audit must confirm the lease actually defines it — capitalised-terms boilerplate does not rescue a term the base agreement never established.

placeholders.name: EquipmentName
placeholders.renders: …operation of the {{EquipmentName}}… → operation of the Communication Facility…
placeholders.note: Communication Facility, Installation, Antenna Facilities, Equipment.

placeholders.name: DocumentType
placeholders.renders: …terminate this {{DocumentType}}… → terminate this Lease…
placeholders.note: Lease, Sublease, License or Sublicense. Drives the recital verb as well as the clause text.

placeholders.name: LeaseDocument
placeholders.renders: …the terms of the {{LeaseDocument}}… → the terms of the Agreement…
placeholders.note: What the base document calls ITSELF. Often just "Agreement", which reads oddly until you check the original and find it never says "Lease Agreement" once.

placeholders.name: Proposed_Amendment
placeholders.source: derived from documentChain — the ordinal of this amendment
placeholders.renders: THIS {{Proposed_Amendment}} TO… → THIS THIRD AMENDMENT TO…
placeholders.note: Counted from the chain, never typed, because stated titles and chronological order disagree often enough that typing it is how the wrong one gets used.

placeholders.name: SiteName
placeholders.renders: …referencing Site {{SiteName}}… → …referencing Site SAMPLE RIDGE…
placeholders.note: As the carrier's records hold it, because that is what a notice clerk will match against.

placeholders.name: FAN
placeholders.renders: …Fixed Asset Number {{FAN}}… → …Fixed Asset Number 10001234…
placeholders.note: Digits only, no label — the clause supplies the words.

placeholders.name: Landlord_Name
placeholders.renders: …by and between {{Landlord_Name}}… → …by and between Springfield Holdings LLC…
placeholders.note: The full legal entity name as it will appear on the signature block, including LLC or Inc. An amendment naming a party differently from the lease it amends is a real defect.

placeholders.name: Landlord_Address
placeholders.renders: …notices to {{Landlord_Address}}… → …notices to 1 Example Road, Springfield, ZZ 00000…
placeholders.note: One line, comma separated, no trailing full stop — the clause punctuates around it.

placeholders.name: Tenant_Notice_Entity
placeholders.renders: …and {{Tenant_Notice_Entity}}… → …and Sample Wireless PCS, LLC…
placeholders.note: The contracting entity, which is often not the brand. Read it off the lease, not off the letterhead.

placeholders.name: Tenant_Notice_Address
placeholders.sample: Attn: Network Real Estate Administration, 100 Example Street, Sample City, ZZ 00000
placeholders.renders: …{{Tenant_Notice_Entity}}, {{Tenant_Notice_Address}}… → …Sample Wireless PCS, LLC, Attn: Network Real Estate Administration, 100 Example Street…
placeholders.note: Include the attention line. A notice that reaches the right building and the wrong desk is a notice not given, and that is how a non-renewal deadline gets missed.

placeholders.name: Governing_Jurisdiction
placeholders.renders: …governed by the laws of {{Governing_Jurisdiction}}… → …governed by the laws of Texas…
placeholders.note: The state NAME, spelled out — not the postal abbreviation. "the laws of TX" is not drafting. Where site.address.state holds an abbreviation, expand it before the amendment goes out.

placeholders.name: Lease_Commencement_Date
placeholders.renders: …dated {{Lease_Commencement_Date}}… → …dated May 1, 2006…
placeholders.note: Stored in the deal file as yyyy-mm-dd and spelled out on the way in. Never type the spelled form — the parser guarantees the two agree.

placeholders.name: Current_Term_End_Date
placeholders.renders: …shall expire on {{Current_Term_End_Date}}… → …shall expire on April 30, 2026…
placeholders.note: The last day of the term now running, not the day after.

placeholders.name: Extension_Term_Start_Date
placeholders.renders: …commencing on {{Extension_Term_Start_Date}}… → …commencing on May 1, 2026…
placeholders.note: Normally the day after Current_Term_End_Date. A gap or an overlap between the two is a drafting error the audit should have caught.

placeholders.name: RentProposal
placeholders.source: the agreed proposal's monthly rent, to two decimals
placeholders.renders: …(${{RentProposal}}) per month… → …($1,950.00) per month…
placeholders.note: DIGITS ONLY, with a thousands separator and two decimals. The clause supplies the dollar sign and the brackets, so a value of "$1,950" renders as "($$1,950)".

placeholders.name: RentProposal_Words
placeholders.sample: one thousand nine hundred fifty dollars
placeholders.renders: {{RentProposal_Words}} (${{RentProposal}}) → one thousand nine hundred fifty dollars ($1,950.00)
placeholders.note: Generated, never typed. Legal drafting states a figure twice and THE WORDS CONTROL where the two disagree, so a hand-typed word form that drifts from the figure means the opposite of what was agreed.

placeholders.name: EscalatorProposal
placeholders.source: the agreed proposal's fixed-percent escalator rate
placeholders.renders: …increase by {{EscalatorProposal}} percent… → …increase by 2 percent…
placeholders.note: The NUMBER only — the clause supplies the word "percent". A value of "2%" renders as "2% percent". Whole numbers only: the word form of a fractional rate is not something anybody drafts.

placeholders.name: EscalatorProposal_Words
placeholders.renders: {{EscalatorProposal_Words}} ({{EscalatorProposal}}%) → two percent (2%)
placeholders.note: Generated. Returns empty for a fractional rate rather than guessing, so the drafter surfaces it instead of emitting something odd.

placeholders.name: Insurance_CGL_Limit
placeholders.renders: …limits of not less than {{Insurance_CGL_Limit}}… → …limits of not less than Three Million Dollars ($3,000,000.00)…
placeholders.note: THE WHOLE PHRASE, words and figure together, because the clause drops it in bare. A value of "3000000" reads as "limits of not less than 3000000".

placeholders.name: Colocation_Share_Pct
placeholders.renders: …a share equal to {{Colocation_Share_Pct}} of… → …a share equal to twenty percent (20%) of…
placeholders.note: Words and figure, like the insurance limit. A bare 20 reads as "a share equal to 20 of the revenue".

placeholders.name: ROFR_Notice_Days
placeholders.renders: …within {{ROFR_Notice_Days}} days… → …within thirty (30) days…
placeholders.note: Words and figure; the clause supplies "days". A bare 30 reads as "within 30 days", which is not wrong but is not how the rest of the document reads.

placeholders.name: RAD_Center_Feet
placeholders.renders: …at a RAD centre of {{RAD_Center_Feet}} feet… → …at a RAD centre of one hundred twenty (120) feet…
placeholders.note: Words and figure; the clause supplies "feet".

placeholders.name: Rent_Guarantee_End_Date
placeholders.renders: …shall not terminate before {{Rent_Guarantee_End_Date}}… → …shall not terminate before September 30, 2031…
placeholders.unusedNote: No clause currently uses this. The rent-guarantee clauses were removed from the library; the resolution and the sample stay so that client-approved guarantee language can be dropped in without re-deriving how the value should be written.
placeholders.note: Spelled out from yyyy-mm-dd, like the other dates.
